title: Grateful Dead Live at The Warehouse on 1970-01-31
lineage: SBD > MR > C > D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording of decent quality captures a rare acoustic‑heavy show with standout gems like Saw Mill, Hard to Handle and Katie May.
ai_review.review: The SBD tape is generally clear with only a little hiss, offering a solid listening base for an otherwise remarkable 1970 concert. Reviewers rave about the acoustic set’s “gold” moments – rare cuts such as Saw Mill, a blistering Hard to Handle and Katie May’s soulful delivery – while noting Phil Lesh’s amp mishap that oddly spurred a special second‑set vibe. A few listeners complained of short song lengths and a generally grumpy mood, but the overwhelming tone is positive.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating is 4.25/5; most comments praise musical highlights and deem the soundboard quality acceptable, with only occasional criticism of amp issues or short songs.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Standard SBD clarity with a bit of hiss; overall acceptable and typical for early‑70 recordings. No major dropouts reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The concert is split between a strong acoustic half that many call “pure gold” and a second set salvaged by Phil’s amp mishap, yielding an unexpectedly inspired performance despite overall shorter song lengths.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar work on Hard to Handle is described as intense and full of anger; tone praised.
band_member_comments.Phil: Amp blew during the show, yet his bass still drove a special second set; reviewers note the mishap turned into “gold”.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen (organ) is highlighted as captivating; likely refers to keyboard duties.
